name: Shop or showroom
description: A brick-and-mortar shop or showroom: products with an enquiry basket instead of a checkout, in-store events and customers' questions, with facts about payment, parking, reserve and collect, returns, delivery and the brands carried.

questions.question: Which brands do you carry?
questions.help: The main ones, separated by commas. Mention an authorised dealer or service status only if the brand has granted it to you.

questions.question: How can customers pay in the shop?
questions.help: For example "cash, cards, mobile payments, meal vouchers".

questions.question: Can customers reserve products through an enquiry and collect them in the shop? For how long do you hold them?
questions.help: For example "we confirm by e-mail and hold the goods for 3 working days". The site has no checkout – the reservation is an enquiry you answer.

questions.question: What are your rules for returns and exchanges?
questions.help: As you state them in the shop, e.g. "exchange within 30 days with the receipt". The law gives buyers rights you cannot limit, and they differ for shop and distance sales – check what applies.

questions.question: Do you deliver or install what customers buy? On what terms?
questions.help: For example "delivery within 30 km for 20 EUR, assembly on request". Leave it empty if customers take everything with them.

questions.question: Where can customers park?
questions.help: For example "free car park in front of the shop, loading space for bulky goods".

questions.question: Can customers in a wheelchair or with a pram get into the shop?
questions.help: Describe it as it is, e.g. "level entrance, all floors by lift" or "two steps at the door, we are glad to help".

questions.question: Since which year has the shop been open?

audit.message: Add your products, or at least the main ranges – people want to know what you sell before they come.
The products have not changed for a year – check what you still sell, the prices and the availability.
Add your opening hours in Business details – customers check them before they set off.
Add the shop's address in Business details – customers navigate by it and search engines show it on the map.
Say how customers can pay in the shop – nobody wants to find out at the till.

claude: People visit a shop's site to learn whether it has what they want, whether it is open now and how to get there – put the opening hours ({{hours.status}}), the address, the main ranges and the brands at the top. Products are the products collection; the site has no checkout and no stock levels, so the Add to enquiry button collects products into an enquiry the shop answers – call it an enquiry or a reservation, never an order or a purchase, and state availability only as the owner gives it. Never invent products, prices, discounts, sales, brands, authorised-dealer status or reviews. Payment, reserve and collect, returns and delivery are facts written as the owner states them; consumer rights differ by country, so say they should be checked rather than stating them as law. A shop with more stores adds the Branches collection.
